I am 66 years old now, and I have farmed this land in Quzhou for 50 years. I know every corner of my 10.1 mu. My wife and I are the only ones living at home—our children work in the city and send money back, but they are not here to help in the fields. So I must be realistic about what two old people can manage. I have a well for irrigation, but pumping water costs electricity, so I do not waste a drop.

My backbone is the wheat-maize rotation on 7 mu. The winter wheat went into the ground last October, as it always does. Now that spring has arrived, I will top-dress it with urea at green-up and irrigate three times from my well: at regreening, at jointing, and at heading. I will spray for powdery mildew and aphids three times. I use an improved wheat variety that I trust—hybrid wheat is too expensive and not necessary here. I expect about 500 kg per mu if the spring drought does not get too severe. As soon as the wheat comes out in early June, I will immediately plant hybrid maize on that same 7 mu. Summer maize is simple: compound fertilizer at planting, sidedress nitrogen at the big-flare stage, irrigate twice during silking and grain-filling, and spray twice for armyworm and ear rot. I should get about 560 kg per mu. I rotary till for both because the turnaround between wheat harvest and maize planting is only a few days.

I keep 2 mu for cotton. It is hard work—picking hurts my back and knees—but the buyers still come, and the income helps. I plough deep for cotton because it likes loose soil. I plant hybrid cotton seed when the soil warms up in late April. Cotton is hungry and thirsty, so I fertilize with NPK and irrigate three times, but the real burden is pests. I spray four times for bollworm, aphids, and mites. I hope for 280 kg of seed cotton per mu.

The remaining 1.1 mu is stevia. I started growing it years ago after a buyer from the county said he would purchase dried leaves. It is less labor than cotton. I rotary till, plant improved seedlings, give it modest fertilizer, irrigate three times, and spray twice for insects. I can harvest about 190 kg of dried leaves per mu.

I do not over-fertilize anymore. After 50 years, I know that throwing more fertilizer at the crops does not always pay back. I use what my experience tells me is enough, and I watch the weather every day.
